title: Keep artifact-name hierarchy and variant depth shallow

facts.note: Task text that involves choosing, reviewing or changing an artifact name.
The planner is the audience; a phase observer is needed to know the planner is making the naming decision.
A name observer can count hierarchy levels and variant dots mechanically; it must inspect every artifact name considered, at any depth, not only new or deeper ones.
Whether each separator adds clear semantic value can only be judged, and applies at any depth.

fires: The planner names an artifact using 4-5 hierarchy levels where fewer would carry the same meaning
The planner names an artifact with more than 5 hierarchy levels
The planner names an artifact with 2 or more variant dots, or more than 2
The planner names an artifact at typical depth (2-3 hierarchy levels, 0-1 dots) but one separator adds no clear semantic value
The planner renames an artifact without changing its depth, and the resulting name contains a separator with no clear semantic value
The planner reviews or keeps an existing artifact name whose depth or separators are being considered
doesNotFire: The work does not involve choosing, reviewing or changing any artifact name
Deciding which separator character expresses which relationship (the separator-semantics convention), as opposed to how deep each goes

given: The planner is choosing or reconsidering an artifact name
when: Deciding how many hierarchy levels and variant (dot) levels the name has
then: Keep hierarchy at 2-3 levels (4-5 max, sparingly) and variants at 0-1 dots (2 max), with each separator adding clear semantic value.
prefer: Remove a separator (and its level) when it does not add clear semantic value
avoid: Hierarchy beyond 5 levels; using 4-5 levels routinely rather than sparingly
More than 2 variant levels; multiple dots often indicate over-specification
Any separator that does not add clear semantic value, at any depth
why: Depth is the recommended nesting per separator; multiple dots often indicate over-specification, so each separator must add clear semantic value.
evidence: Each artifact name considered has at most 5 hierarchy levels and at most 2 variant levels
4-5 hierarchy levels are used sparingly, not as the norm
For every separator in the name, its semantic value can be stated
verifier_detail: Term 'depth' = the recommended nesting depth per separator
Thresholds: hierarchy_typical=2-3 levels; hierarchy_maximum=4-5 levels (use sparingly); variant_typical=0-1 levels; variant_maximum=2 levels
Warning: multiple dots often indicate over-specification
Variant levels are counted as dots; hierarchy levels are counted using the hierarchy separator defined by the separator-semantics convention
